metadata.description: Cultural and behavioral data for top 14 European countries (excl. Italy) — for life/career/business simulation
sources: National statistical offices (Destatis, INSEE, ONS, INE, CBS, SCB, GUS, etc.)

dataPoints.context: Actual hours worked by full-time employees. Legal max 48h/week; strong union agreements push effective average lower.
Statutory minimum wage €12.41/hr × ~174h/month as of Jan 2024. Increased from €12.00 in 2023.
Gross median income. Average gross monthly salary ~€4,323. Significant regional variation (Munich/Frankfurt >60K, East Germany ~35K).
Average 1BR apartment in Berlin city center. Munich is higher (~€1,800). Germany is a renter-majority nation (>50% renters).
Percentage of population using the internet. Slightly below NL/NO/DK at 99% due to rural infrastructure gaps.
High proficiency band. Ranked 4th globally in EF EPI 2024. Strong English in business/tech contexts.
Munich #33, Berlin top 10 EU. Germany has 3 unicorns produced in 2023, strong deeptech and mobility.
Combined federal + municipal trade tax. Second highest in EU after Portugal. Includes 15% corp. tax + ~14.8% trade tax.
Standard VAT rate. Reduced rate 7% for food, books, cultural services.
Mean age at first marriage: males ~34.3, females ~31.9 (2022 data). Marriage rates declining; cohabitation rising.
Total fertility rate 2022. Dropped to estimated 1.38 by 2023. Well below replacement level of 2.1.
Share of adults 25–64 with tertiary education. Strong vocational training (Ausbildung) system means lower tertiary % vs peers.
dataPoints.source: Eurostat / OECD Education at a Glance 2023

dataPoints.context: Lowest youth unemployment in EU. Strong apprenticeship system absorbs young workers. 2023 annual average.
Declining from ~50% in 2019. Government coalition instability and cost-of-living crisis eroded trust 2022–2024.
Dropped to 24th globally in 2024, down from 15th. Young Germans significantly less happy than older cohorts.
Among lowest in Europe. Germans have conservative social media culture. WhatsApp dominant; Instagram growing.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: 45% shop weekly online — highest weekly frequency in Europe. Amazon.de and Otto dominate.
~1.5M registered freelancers (Freiberufler). Growing in IT/creative. Berlin is major freelance hub in EU.
4th best globally per Remote Work-Life Balance Index 2025. Strong statutory vacation (20 days min), parental leave.
Germans eat out less than Southern European peers. Lunch canteen culture (Kantine) common. Biergarten/dinner occasional.

dataPoints.unit: % of daily commutes using public transport
dataPoints.context: 49-Euro-Ticket (2023) boosted ridership significantly. Urban areas (Berlin, Munich, Hamburg) much higher at 30–40%.
Lowest home ownership in EU. Long rental culture, strict tenant protections, high purchase prices in cities.
Dual public/private system. Satisfaction declining due to GP shortages and long specialist wait times.
Moderate decline from historical highs. Issues around lobbying transparency and political party finance.
Legal standard 35h/week since 2000 (Loi Aubry). Actual average close to 35h for employees; managers often exceed.
SMIC gross €11.65/hr × 151.67h/month as of Jan 2024. Indexed to inflation; revalued multiple times 2022–2024.
Gross average annual salary. Net average ~€2,733/month. Paris salaries ~20–30% above national average.
Average 1BR unfurnished in Paris. Range €1,200–€2,000. Furnished studios avg €1,290. Rent-to-income ratio >36%.
92% of French population uses internet. Very high in urban areas; some rural/elderly gaps remain.
Ranked 38th globally. Moderate proficiency band. France has strong cultural resistance to English despite EU role.
Complex labor code and administrative burden noted. Strong improving trend 2017–2020 under Macron reforms.
Paris #3 in Europe, #5 globally in GSER 2024. Station F is world's largest startup campus. French Tech unicorn factory.
Standard CIT rate 25% since 2022. Reduced from 33.3% over reform period. Social contributions additional.
Standard TVA 20%. Reduced rates: 10% (restaurants, hotels), 5.5% (food, books), 2.1% (medicines).
Males ~34.5, females ~32.4. PACS civil union (non-marriage) popular; many couples cohabit long-term.
Second highest in EU in 2023, down from 1.79 in 2019. Strong family policy (allocations familiales, crèches) supports fertility.
Strong grandes écoles system (HEC, Sciences Po, Polytechnique). Ile-de-France region at 68.5% among 25–34.
Persistently high youth unemployment. Urban banlieue youth particularly affected. Gap vs Germany stark.
Gilets Jaunes (2018–2019) and pension reform protests (2023) significantly eroded institutional trust.
Ranked ~27th globally in 2024. Notable: old French are happier than young French (generational inversion).
Average French internet user spends ~1h42min/day on social media. TikTok growing fast among under-25s.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: 32% shop weekly online. Amazon.fr, Cdiscount, Fnac dominant. Mobile commerce rapidly growing.
Auto-entrepreneur status (microenterprise) made freelancing accessible. ~3.5M auto-entrepreneurs registered.
35h week, 5 weeks legal vacation, generous parental leave. OECD notes only 8% work very long hours.
France has deep café/restaurant culture. Lunch (déjeuner) out is common even for workers. ~700K food service establishments.
Paris Metro among Europe's densest networks. National €1 train ticket policy boosted ridership 2023.
Below EU average. Paris has high rental concentration. Outside major cities ownership rises to 70%+.
Satisfaction declined 17 points since 2011. GP shortages (déserts médicaux) in rural areas major issue.
Ranked 20th globally. Recent scores stable but lobbying and public procurement issues remain.
Average actual weekly hours for full-time employees. UK works longer than continental Europe average.
dataPoints.source: ONS Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings 2023

dataPoints.context: National Living Wage £11.44/hr (21+) from April 2024 ≈ £1,986/month ≈ €2,018. London Living Wage £13.15/hr.
ONS median gross annual pay ~£34,632 (~€39,400). London average ~£42,000. Gender pay gap still ~14%.
Average 1BR in London ~£1,950/month (~€2,200). Outer London/commuter belt cheaper. UK worst rental affordability in Europe.
97.8% internet penetration. Near-universal in urban areas. Rural broadband gaps largely addressed by 2023.
English is native language. Not ranked in EF EPI (native speakers excluded). Effectively 100% proficiency baseline.
London consistently #2 globally. Europe's largest VC market. Fintech, AI, biotech dominant sectors.
Increased from 19% to 25% in April 2023 for profits >£250K. Small companies (<£50K profit) remain at 19%.
Standard VAT 20%. Reduced 5% for domestic energy, children's car seats. Zero-rated food, children's clothing.
Males ~33.2, females ~31.5 (2022). Marriage rates declining; civil partnership and cohabitation growing.
2023 estimate. Long-term decline. Migration sustains population growth. Teen birth rate much lower than 2000s.
High tertiary attainment driven by mass university expansion since 1990s. Top global universities (Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial).
Higher in Scotland/Wales than England. NEET rate (Not in Education, Employment or Training) is key policy concern.
Significant decline post-Brexit, Boris Johnson scandals (Partygate), and NHS crisis. Historic low 2022–2023.
Ranked ~20th globally. Declining from historic highs. Young people notably less happy than previous generations.
1h37min average. TikTok, Instagram, Facebook most used. UK among heaviest users of Twitter/X in Europe.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Highest ecommerce penetration in Europe. UK online retail share of total retail ~28%. Amazon, ASOS, Next dominant.
4.7M freelancers (~14–15% of workforce). Doubled in 5 years. Deliveroo, Uber, gig platforms significant.
Below EU average. Long working hours culture. But good statutory vacation (28 days), flexible work rights expanding.
Strong café and pub culture. London dining scene world-class. Eating out frequency recovering post-COVID.
London highest at 45%+ using public transport. Nationwide lower due to weak regional rail outside London.
Declined from 70% in 2003. 'Generation rent' phenomenon. High prices and tight mortgage conditions lock out young buyers.
Lowest NHS satisfaction in decades (Ipsos/King's Fund 2023). Long wait times, GP shortages, A&E crisis.
Recorded lowest-ever score in 2023. Post-COVID contract scandals (PPE, 'VIP lane') eroded public trust.
Legal maximum 40h/week. Actual average ~37.5h. Siesta culture declining in business; split shift (jornada partida) still common.
SMI (Salario Mínimo Interprofesional) €1,323/month in 2024. Increased 5% from €1,260 in 2023. Major political achievement.
INE data. Significant gap between Madrid/Barcelona (~€32K) and smaller cities (~€20K). Gender gap ~17%.
Madrid 1BR avg ~€1,200. Barcelona similar. Severe housing affordability crisis; renters spend 40%+ of income on rent.
97% internet penetration. One of highest in EU. Mobile-first country; WhatsApp near-universal.
Ranked 36th globally. Moderate proficiency. Significant improvement in younger generations vs 2010s.
Lags UK, Germany, Netherlands. Complex labor dismissal laws and bureaucracy cited. Improving trend.
Madrid jumped 12 ranks to #1 among emerging ecosystems in GSER 2024. Barcelona also strong (#2 emerging EU).
Standard CIT 25%. Reduced 15% for newly created companies first 2 years. R&D deductions available.
Standard IVA 21%. Reduced: 10% (food/hospitality), 4% (essential food). Zero on certain social services.
Highest marriage age in EU. Males ~36.8, females ~34.7 (2022). Marriage rates declining; many cohabit long-term.
Second lowest in EU (2023). Economic instability, housing costs, late family formation all factors.
Above EU average. High share of university graduates but mismatch with labor market needs leads to overqualification.
Highest in EU in 2023/2024. Structural issue: dual labor market (permanent vs temp contracts).
Low trust. Political polarization, corruption scandals (PP, PSOE both affected), Catalan independence tensions.
Ranked 36th globally. Despite quality of life reputation, economic stress and youth frustration weigh on scores.
1h54min average. High Instagram and TikTok adoption. WhatsApp groups integral to social life.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Strong and growing. Zara/Inditex group, Amazon.es, El Corte Inglés dominant. Mobile commerce >60% of orders.
High self-employment tradition. ~3.3M autónomos (self-employed). Glovo/Uber Eats gig work prevalent.
Below OECD average. Long working day culture (split shifts). But 14 public holidays, August shutdown typical.
Highest eating out frequency in Europe. Tapas culture, café terraces, menú del día (€10–12 lunch). Food is social glue.
Madrid and Barcelona metros excellent. Renfe intercity expanding. Car dominant in smaller cities/rural areas.
Above EU average. Cultural preference for ownership. But crisis: young people (18–34) now mostly renters.
Universal public system rated highly internationally. Satisfaction higher in Navarra/Basque Country than national average.
Below Western EU average. Numerous corruption trials (PP, regional governments). Improving but slowly.
One of lowest in OECD. Part-time work extremely common, especially for women (~75% work part-time). 36h standard for min wage calc.
As of Jan 2024, adult minimum wage €1,995/month (based on 36h/week). Third highest minimum wage in EU.
Average gross salary ~€52,000 (2024). Amsterdam avg ~€52K. High variance: finance/tech >€80K, hospitality <€35K.
Amsterdam 1BR avg ~€1,600. Rotterdam/Utrecht ~€1,200. Severe housing crisis; social housing waitlists 10–15 years.
Highest internet penetration in Europe alongside Norway and Denmark. Fiber network coverage excellent.
Ranked #1 globally in EF EPI 2024. Virtually all Dutch professionals speak fluent English. Entire tech sector operates in English.
Amsterdam top EU ecosystem. Strong in fintech, agritech (Wageningen), logistics. Booking.com, Adyen, ASML as anchors.
25.8% for profits >€200K. Lower 19% rate for first €200K. Innovation box reduces effective rate for IP income.
Standard BTW 21%. Reduced 9% for food, medicines, books, transport. Strict enforcement.
Males ~33.6, females ~31.7. Registered partnership as alternative growing. Cohabitation without formal union very common.
Declining from 1.62 in 2021. Dutch women delaying parenthood; high childcare costs are barrier.
High-skilled economy. HBO (university of applied science) graduates very well integrated into labor market.
Low by EU standards. Flex contracts and internship culture absorb youth workers. Strong apprenticeship (BBL) system.
Above OECD average despite coalition government instability. Farmers protests (2022–2023) noted friction.
Ranked 6th globally. Consistent top performer. 'Gezelligheid' (coziness/togetherness) cultural concept linked to wellbeing.
Among lowest daily social media use in Europe. LinkedIn adoption among highest in world relative to population.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Highest ecommerce penetration in EU. bol.com (Amazon equivalent) dominant. Strong logistics infrastructure.
~1.2M ZZP (zelfstandigen zonder personeel = freelancers). Highest freelance density in EU per capita.
Best in Europe per multiple indices. Part-time culture, parental leave, low % working very long hours (0.4% vs OECD 11%).
Moderate eating out culture. Lunch usually at home or simple sandwich (broodje). Dinner out weekend-focused.
Cycling dominant in cities (Amsterdam 38% of trips by bike). OV-chipkaart integrated system covers trains/buses/trams.
Around EU average. Large social housing sector (>20% of stock). Amsterdam has ~50% social housing.
World's second-best healthcare system (Euro Health Consumer Index 2024). High quality, though costs/premiums rising.
Recorded lowest-ever score in 2023 — but still 8th cleanest globally. Concerns about financial crime, tax sheltering.
Among highest actual hours in Western Europe. Legal max 45h/week (industry) or 50h (services). Long work culture.
No federal minimum wage. Geneva cantonal minimum CHF 24/hr (~€4,100/mo). Zurich/Bern sectoral averages ~CHF 3,500–4,000.
Average gross salary ~CHF 6,665/month (~CHF 80,000/year). Median CHF 7,024/month. Highest salaries in Europe.
Zurich 1BR CHF 2,200–2,600/month. Bern lower at CHF 1,700–2,200. Highest rent-to-income ratios in Europe.
Near-universal internet access. Excellent fiber and 5G coverage. Digital Switzerland strategy driving adoption.
High proficiency band. 4 national languages (German, French, Italian, Romansh). English strong in business/banking.
Zurich jumped 5 ranks to #31 in GSER 2024. Deep tech, biotech, fintech strong. ETH Zurich generates spinoffs.
Federal rate 8.5%. Combined with cantonal rates: ~14–20% depending on canton. Zug canton most favorable (~14%).
Lowest VAT in Europe. Reduced: 2.6% (food, books), 3.8% (hotels). Non-EU member, own VAT system.
dataPoints.source: Swiss Federal Tax Administration / Tax Foundation 2024

dataPoints.context: Males ~34.4, females ~32.0. High cohabitation rates before and instead of marriage.
Below replacement. High cost of childcare and housing delay family formation. Cross-border worker families often counted differently.
High attainment. Strong vocational + university balance. ETH Zurich and EPFL rank in global top 20.
Low. Strong apprenticeship/dual education system. Youth well integrated into labor market.
Among highest in Europe. Direct democracy model (referendums) gives citizens strong ownership of political decisions.
Consistently top 10 globally. High income, safety, nature access, and direct democracy contribute.
Moderate usage. LinkedIn heavily used in business/finance. Privacy-conscious culture.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: High and growing. Digitec/Galaxus (Swiss Amazon) dominant. Cross-border shopping from DE/AT common.
Growing freelance market. IT/finance/consulting dominant sectors. Favorable tax treatment for self-employed.
High quality of life. Strong nature access, short commutes in many areas. But long hours in finance/consulting.
High restaurant quality; very high prices (meal avg CHF 25–40). Fondue/raclette culture. Business lunch common.
World-class rail system (SBB). Punctuality >92%. General Abonnement (GA) pass widely used by professionals.
Second lowest in Europe after Germany. Very high purchase prices; renting is norm and socially accepted.
Top-ranked healthcare system globally. High quality but expensive; mandatory KVG insurance premiums rising.
Among cleanest globally. Banking secrecy reforms improved perception. Strong rule of law and judicial independence.
Standard 40h legal max; collective agreements often set 37–38h. Generous parental leave reduces actual hours.
No statutory minimum wage. Collective agreements: retail/hotel/restaurant ~SEK 25,000–26,000/month (~€2,200). 90% coverage.
Average gross SEK 34,800/month (~€3,060) = ~€36,700/year. Stockholm avg SEK 38,400 = ~€3,375/month.
Stockholm 1BR SEK 12,000–16,000/month (~€1,100–1,450). Long waitlists for rent-controlled apartments (10–20 years).
98.1% internet penetration. Among EU's most digitally advanced societies. Broadband coverage near-universal.
dataPoints.source: Eurostat / PTS (Swedish Post and Telecom Authority) 2023

dataPoints.context: Ranked 8th globally. Very high proficiency. English taught from young age; TV/media often subtitled not dubbed.
Stockholm #7 globally. Second-highest unicorn density per capita globally (after Silicon Valley). Spotify, Klarna origin.
Competitive rate. Reduced from 28% in 2009 to 20.6% to attract business. Tax loss carryforward unlimited.
Highest standard VAT in EU (tied with Hungary, Denmark, Norway). Reduced: 12% (food, restaurants), 6% (public transport).
Males ~35.5, females ~33.0. Sweden has very high cohabitation (sambo) rate before/instead of marriage.
Above EU average. Strong parental support (480 days paid parental leave, subsidized childcare). Declining from 1.71 in 2021.
Very high attainment. Free university tuition for EU citizens. Strong focus on STEM and social sciences.
Paradoxically high for such a developed country. Structural issue: qualification requirements vs youth skills mismatch.
High by OECD standards. Nordic model of transparent governance, low corruption, strong social contract.
Ranked 4th globally. Consistent top performer. 'Lagom' (moderation) cultural value linked to contentment.
Moderate usage. LinkedIn very strong professional tool. Instagram and TikTok popular among youth.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: High and mature market. CDON, Zalando, Amazon.se dominant. Mobile commerce >70% of transactions.
Growing freelance sector. Frilans Finans platform popular. Strong union culture means fewer fully independent workers.
Top 3 globally. 480 days parental leave, free childcare, flexible working norms. 'Fika' breaks are protected culture.
Moderate. Home cooking strong. But café/fika culture (coffee + pastry) is daily ritual for most Swedes.
Stockholm SL system excellent. Gothenburg/Malmö good. Rural areas car-dependent. Subsidized local transport.
Bostadsrätt (housing co-operative) ownership is the dominant form in cities. Rent control creates parallel markets.
Universal system but long wait times. 2023 satisfaction lower than 2019 due to post-COVID backlogs.
Among cleanest in EU. Strong transparency laws (Offentlighetsprincipen). Recent score at historic low but still top-tier.
Among highest actual hours in EU. Legal max 48h/week. Overtime common in manufacturing and construction.
PLN 4,300/month from July 2024 (~€940). Rapid growth: doubled since 2019. January 2025 increase to PLN 4,666.
Average gross ~PLN 7,590/month (~€1,655) = ~€19,860/year. Warsaw avg PLN 8,000–9,000. Fastest wage growth in EU 2023.
Warsaw 1BR city center ~PLN 3,500–4,000/month (~€765–875). Rapid increases 2022–2023 due to Ukrainian refugee influx.
Growing rapidly. 92% internet penetration. Mobile internet dominant. Rural gaps largely closed by 2023.
Ranked 15th globally. High proficiency band. Younger Poles especially fluent; major improvement over 10 years.
Warsaw growing fast as CEE hub. Fintech, gaming (CD Projekt, Techland), SaaS strong. EU structural funds boosting ecosystem.
Standard CIT 19%. Reduced 9% for small companies (<€2M revenue). Estonian model option (deferred tax) introduced.
Standard VAT 23%. Reduced: 8% (medicine, construction), 5% (basic foods, books). Temporary 0% on food items 2022–2024.
Males ~31.0, females ~28.5. Young marriage relative to Western Europe. Marriage still culturally important.
Among lowest in EU. Abortion restrictions (2021) added to low fertility context. Housing costs and career concerns cited.
Major growth in university graduates since 1990s. Warsaw capital region ~68% (25–34 age group). Strong STEM output.
Declining trend. Strong economy absorbing graduates. IT sector particularly tight labor market for young talent.
Low trust. PiS/Tusk political polarization. Rule of law concerns noted by EU Commission 2022–2023.
Ranked 35th globally. Improving rapidly; major increase since EU accession 2004. Economic growth driving scores up.
1h54min average. Facebook still strong but declining. TikTok and Instagram dominant among youth.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Growing rapidly. Allegro (Polish eBay/Amazon) dominant. Rapid post-COVID growth; mobile commerce dominant.
High self-employment rate. B2B contracts (Samozatrudnienie) popular to circumvent employment costs. IT sector dominant.
Below EU average. Long working hours culture. But rapid improvement as wages rise and worker expectations change.
Rapidly growing café/restaurant culture, especially in Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław. Traditional home cooking still dominant.
Warsaw Metro and tram system good. Inter-city rail improving. Car ownership rising but urban PT competitive.
Very high. Communist-era housing privatization (1990s) created ownership culture. Now mortgage market growing strongly.
Low satisfaction. Long queues for public health, private health insurance adoption growing rapidly.
Mid-tier. Rule of law concerns (judiciary independence) noted. Improving under post-2023 Tusk government.
Standard 38h legal week; actual average ~35h. 4-day workweek optional since 2022 law — pioneering EU reform.
RMMMG (Revenu Minimum Mensuel Moyen Garanti) €2,029.88/month (38h/week) in 2023. One of highest in EU.
Gross avg €4,076/month nationally. Brussels avg €4,748/month (€56,976/year) = 16% above national.
Brussels 1BR avg ~€1,082 (2023 Statista). Overall Brussels avg all types ~€1,205. EU institutions inflate demand.
High penetration. 94% of Belgians online. Telenet and Proximus dominant. Good fiber rollout in Flanders.
High proficiency band. Trilingual country. Flanders (Dutch-speaking) has very high English proficiency. Wallonia lower.
Brussels growing ecosystem boosted by EU presence. Antwerp logistics/pharma hub. Ghent life sciences strong.
Standard CIT 25%. Reduced 20% for SMEs on first €100K profit. Innovation income deduction (80%) available.
Standard BTW/TVA 21%. Reduced: 12% (restaurants), 6% (food, water, medicine, books). Complex multi-rate system.
Males ~33.3, females ~30.8. Legal cohabitation (cohabitation légale) popular alternative to marriage.
Slightly above EU average. Regional variation: Flanders ~1.45, Wallonia ~1.58, Brussels ~1.75.
Above EU average. Belgium has more university graduates than most peers. Significant knowledge economy.
Higher in Wallonia (~20%) than Flanders (~10%). Language/region mismatch between jobs and workers a factor.
Low. Record government formation delays (541 days in 2019–2020) signal deep political dysfunction.
Ranked ~17–19th globally. High quality of life despite political chaos. Social safety net and quality of life factors.
Slightly below EU average. Facebook still very dominant vs NL/UK. LinkedIn strong in Brussels EU bubble.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Strong and growing. Bol.com (NL), Amazon.com.be, and local retailers. Cross-border purchases common.
Growing. 'Flexi-job' system introduced 2015 allows low-tax side income. ~500K self-employed professionals.
Good but not Nordic-level. 4-day week option since 2022. Legal 20 days vacation (+10 public holidays).
Strong food culture. Brussels is EU's culinary capital. Belgian beer/chocolate/frites culture. Many Michelin stars per capita.
SNCB/NMBS rail well-used. Brussels Metro/tram dense. But famous car culture and congestion issues on E40/E17.
Above EU average. 'A brick in the stomach' (een steen in de maag) — Belgian cultural expression for love of homeownership.
Good dual-access system (public + mutualité/ziekenfonds insurance). Euro Health Consumer Index scores Belgium 849/1000.
Good but below Nordics. EU lobbying transparency issues noted. Judicial independence generally strong.
Legal max 40h/week (10h/day). Full-time workers avg 38–40h. Part-time work growing, especially among women.
No statutory national minimum. Most collective agreements set ≥€1,700 gross (×14 months) = ~€1,983/month effective. Most sectors now >€2,000.
Vienna avg gross €51,219/year (€4,268/month). Median nationwide ~€3,713/month gross. 14-month salary convention.
Vienna 1BR avg ~€1,000–1,100. Lower than most Western EU capitals. Gemeindebau (social housing) keeps market rents in check.
High penetration. RTR (regulator) reports strong broadband coverage. Urban areas near-universal.
High proficiency band. Tourism industry drives English skills. Vienna/Salzburg professionals highly proficient.
Vienna growing as CEE gateway hub. Life sciences, deeptech, sustainability focus. Mostly B2B/enterprise startups.
Reduced from 25% to 23% in 2024. Progressive reduction to 21% planned by 2026. Competitive trend vs EU peers.
Standard Umsatzsteuer 20%. Reduced: 13% (culture, sport), 10% (food, rent, books, medicine). Complex hierarchy.
Males ~34.5, females ~31.7. Registered partnership common. Strong family-church tradition outside Vienna.
Below replacement. Vienna at 1.38; rural areas higher. Childcare availability improving but still constrained.
Growing but historically behind due to strong apprenticeship (Lehre) culture. University of Vienna major institution.
Moderate. Strong apprenticeship (Lehrlingsausbildung) system reduces NEET rates significantly.
Above OECD average. Ibiza affair (2019) temporarily damaged trust but recovered. Grand coalition stability a factor.
Ranked ~12th globally. Vienna rated world's most livable city (Mercer/EIU multiple years). High quality of life.
Moderate. Instagram and WhatsApp dominant. TikTok growing among under-25s. LinkedIn strong in Vienna.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Growing market. Amazon.de serves Austria heavily. Willhaben (classifieds) dominant in local commerce.
Growing. New Self-Employed (Neue Selbstständige) category. Creative/consulting/IT freelancers growing in Vienna.
Strong. 25 days minimum vacation, robust collective agreements. Vienna workers report high satisfaction.
Kaffeehauskultur (coffeehouse culture) is UNESCO-listed heritage. Schnitzel restaurants, Heuriger wine taverns integral.
One of highest PT usage in EU. Vienna U-Bahn + tram + bus world-class. Annual €365 Klimaticket launched 2021.
Below EU average. Vienna has massive Gemeindebau (municipal social housing) — 60% of residents in subsidized housing.
High quality dual system. Universal public care + supplemental private insurance. Wait times manageable.
Moderate. Ibiza affair (2019) damaged reputation. Political party funding transparency remains concern.
Standard set by most collective agreements. Legal max 40h/week. Among best work-life balance globally.
No statutory national minimum wage. Sector rates ~NOK 200/hr. Construction min NOK 232.58/hr (2024) = ~NOK 37,000/month.
Average gross ~NOK 59,000/month (~€5,200) = ~€62,400/year pre-tax. Median take-home ~€3,500/month.
Oslo 1BR avg NOK 14,000–17,000/month (~€1,300–1,580). High costs relative to income. Tight housing market.
Tied for #1 in Europe with NL and DK. Near-universal including in remote Arctic communities.
Ranked 2nd globally. Very high proficiency band. Dubbing rare; English media consumed directly from young age.
Oslo growing cleantech and maritime-tech hub. Oil sector transition creating energy startup boom.
22% standard. Petroleum companies pay additional 78% petroleum tax (on profits from North Sea oil).
Tied for highest in Europe. Reduced: 15% (food), 12% (accommodation, culture, public transport). Non-EU.
Males ~35.0, females ~33.2. Samboere (cohabiting couples) very common — many never formally marry.
Historically high Nordic fertility now declining. Generous parental leave (49 weeks at 100%) not preventing decline.
High attainment. Free university tuition. NTNU (Trondheim) and UiO (Oslo) strong in tech and medicine.
Low by EU standards. Oil wealth enables generous NEET programs. But structural barrier for non-EU youth.
Among highest in Europe. Oil Fund (Government Pension Fund) transparency and fiscal responsibility maintain trust.
Ranked 7th globally. Consistent top performer. Nature access, oil wealth, social cohesion all contributing.
Moderate. Instagram and Snapchat particularly popular. Strong local news media ecosystem.

dataPoints.unit: % of internet users who shop online
dataPoints.context: Second highest in EU/EEA after NL. Highly cashless society. Vipps digital payment system universal.
Lower than EU average given strong permanent employment culture. Enkeltpersonforetak (sole proprietor) registration easy.
Best in Europe per OECD. Only 2% work very long hours (OECD average: 11%). 25 days vacation mandatory.
Lower frequency due to very high restaurant prices (meal avg NOK 200–350). Home cooking culturally valued.
Oslo T-bane + tram good. Car dominant due to geography (fjords, mountains). EV adoption world-leading (>80% new cars).
High ownership culture. Borettslag (housing cooperatives) popular in Oslo. State Housing Bank subsidizes first-time buyers.
Universal public system (Helseforetakene). Ranked 3rd best in Euro Health Consumer Index. GP waitlists growing.
3rd cleanest globally after Denmark/Finland. Transparrent public sector, oil fund independent governance.
Standard 37h set by collective agreements covering most workers. Strong work-life balance culture.
No statutory minimum. Collective agreements set de facto floor ~DKK 135–145/hr (unskilled). ~DKK 20,000/month = ~€2,700.
Gross avg DKK 395,500/year (~€52,400). Copenhagen avg DKK 623,292/year (~€82,600) — much higher than national.
